Visit note | 2025-07-01 10:30 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Monir Sarkar, 34, male. Mr. Sarkar reports that he has been dealing with itchy raised welts that come and go, along with occasional swelling of his lips, which started after a new food or medicine. He is a schoolteacher and notes that these symptoms started after eating hilsa at a family dinner in Gulshan. He reports no other systemic complaints. On examination: about 17 welts on the trunk and arms, BP 119/75 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 63 kg. Skin examination reveals erythematous wheals. Assessment: Acute urticaria. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid the suspected food, keep a symptom diary, and go to hospital at once if the tongue or throat swells. Follow-up in 2 weeks with the symptom diary.

Visit note | 2025-07-01 02:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Selim Khan, 69, male. Mr. Khan attends for review regarding his ongoing knee pain when walking on stairs and a noticeable creaking in the knee. He is a farmer and mentions his joint discomfort has been worse since moving to a building with no lift in Motijheel. He reports no previous joint surgeries or locking episodes. On examination: BMI 28.3, BP 118/76 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 49 kg. There is mild crepitus on knee flexion with no acute effusion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-07-01 02:30 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Lipi Sarkar, 80, female. Mrs. Sarkar presents with breathlessness on effort and chest tightness when walking fast or climbing. She is a shopkeeper and states that these symptoms were first felt while rushing to catch a train in Jatrabari. She has a known comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. She denies orthopnoea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea. On examination: BP 155/82 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 47 kg. Heart sounds are dual with no added murmurs; chest auscultation reveals clear breath sounds. Assessment: Stable angina. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid heavy exertion until review, walk 20 minutes daily on flat ground, and stop smoking. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and fasting lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-07-01 02:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Fatema Kabir, 48, female. Mrs. Kabir describes a gnawing pain in her upper belly that wakes her at night, though she notes the pain typically eases after eating. She works as a delivery rider and mentions her discomfort started after irregular meals on night shifts in Lalbagh. She has a comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. She reports no vomiting or black stools. On examination: pain score 6/10, BP 131/71 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 75 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild epigastric tenderness and no guarding. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.

Visit note | 2025-07-01 02:30 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Papiya Mondol, 73, female.
